title: More visitors at the watering hole
claim: At least 27% of U.S. employer businesses will report recent AI use in the final Census reference window wholly within Q1 2027.
baseline: 24.6% in September 21–October 4, 2026, from the October 22 release; this window crosses quarters. The final wholly within-quarter readings were 19.1% for Q1, 21.7% for Q2 and 23.8% for Q3 2026. These are snapshots, not quarter averages.
rationale: The earlier readings suggest adoption is spreading. A 27% threshold asks whether that direction continues at a modest pace.
risk: Trials may stall, budgets may tighten, or businesses may find less recurring value than expected.
rule: Use the Census Business Trends and Outlook Survey national estimate for AI use in the last two weeks, retaining the current employer-business population and question. Select the final reference window wholly inside January–March 2027. Yes at 27% or above; no below. The published point estimate decides the event; report its standard error separately. Missing data or a changed definition is unresolvable.

title: The forager learns to recover
claim: At least two of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google/DeepMind, Meta and Mistral will publish qualifying new agent-reliability reports during Q1 2027.
baseline: October release notes already emphasize agents and computer-based work. The existing E-02 pilot asks a related question about the remainder of 2026; it is a separate forecast with a different window.
rationale: As agents handle longer sequences, recovering after an error and checking completed work become useful selling points.
risk: Providers may emphasize other capabilities, publish no usable comparison, or describe an aspiration rather than a new result.
rule: Count each named provider once for a dated January–March 2027 release note or technical evaluation concerning a newly released model or agent version. It must explicitly report improvement over an identified earlier version in error recovery, preserving task state, or checking completed work. Google and DeepMind count as one. Reposts and vague promises do not count. Yes with at least two qualifying providers, no with fewer after reviewing the public record. This measures published claims, not independent confirmation of performance.

title: The old river still carries trade
claim: Alphabet will report positive year-over-year growth in Google Search & other revenue for the quarter ending March 31, 2027.
baseline: The recorded Q3 2026 Search & other revenue was $63.350 billion, with 12% reported annual growth, versus 17% growth in Q2. These are company figures.
rationale: An incumbent can retain a growing business while users experiment with alternative ways to find answers.
risk: Advertising weakness, changing discovery habits or pricing pressure could outweigh that resilience.
rule: Use Alphabet’s Q1 2027 results, comparing Google Search & other revenue with the same release’s comparable Q1 2026 figure. Yes if revenue is strictly higher, no if equal or lower. A discontinued or incompatible measure, or no eligible release by cutoff, is unresolvable. The test concerns company revenue, not AI’s causal effect.

title: More channels through the delta
claim: ChatGPT’s share of worldwide, all-platform AI-chatbot referrals in Statcounter will be below 70% in December 2027.
baseline: The September 2026 snapshot was 80.47%, retrieved October 30. It is a share of tracked, identifiable visits sent by AI chatbots to websites, not a share of chatbot users or questions.
rationale: More competing assistants could distribute outbound visits across a wider set of services.
risk: A leading assistant could retain its advantage; tracking changes could also distort the apparent distribution.
rule: Use Statcounter’s December 2027 worldwide, all-platform AI-chatbot referral share after the 45-day revision window, captured by March 31, 2028. Yes below 70%; no at or above. Retain the same source and denominator; an incompatible definition or unavailable observation is unresolvable. A falling share can accompany rising absolute visits.

title: A larger year-round population
claim: At least 35% of U.S. employer businesses will report recent AI use in the final Census reference window wholly within Q4 2027.
baseline: The same 24.6% September 21–October 4, 2026 observation anchors Q01. This annual forecast and Q01 follow the same adoption process; they are related bets, not independent evidence.
rationale: Wider availability and changes to everyday workflows could make recurring use more common over a full year.
risk: The easier uses may already be adopted; integration, trust and cost could slow the next wave.
rule: Apply Q01’s Census population, question and point-estimate rule to the final reference window wholly inside October–December 2027. Yes at 35% or above; no below. Use evidence published by March 31, 2028. Missing data or a changed definition is unresolvable.

title: Some old residents adapt
claim: At least two of Salesforce, ServiceNow and Adobe will report positive year-over-year total revenue growth for their last fiscal quarter ending within calendar 2027.
baseline: The latest recorded annual growth rates were 11% for Salesforce’s quarter ending July 31, 20.5% for ServiceNow’s quarter ending September 30, and 13% for Adobe’s quarter ending August 28, 2026. Their reporting calendars differ.
rationale: Established software businesses can add AI, retain distribution and sell new capabilities while competitors attack parts of their market.
risk: Price pressure, fewer paid accounts, weaker spending or new substitutes could offset those advantages.
rule: For each of the three named companies, select its last fiscal quarter with an end date in calendar 2027. Compare reported total revenue with the same release’s prior-year comparable. Yes if at least two are strictly higher; no otherwise. All three compatible releases must be public by March 31, 2028, or this forecast is unresolvable. Acquisitions must be disclosed; growth does not establish an AI benefit or describe the whole software sector.
